name: sieve
description: Per-customer decision classifiers: each question is served by djev, GLiNER or a tiny fine-tuned model, whichever passes the per-question holdout gate. Every CLI command and HTTP route is declared here (SPEC.md §0). A tool's `run` is its only handler: the CLI and HTTP routes are the doors, and there is no second code path.

conventions.python: Use .venv/bin/python for any tool that loads a model (eval, release, label, serve, ab.run, tiny.*). python3 is enough for status, init, import, check, rollback and ab.report.
conventions.output: Each CLI prints one final line `verdict=<CLASS> key=value ...` (stderr on failure). Bounded: one line per customer or per question, never per row.

exit.2: SETUP: missing customer, unreachable service, wrong python; the message names the command that fixes it

conventions.delegable: agent = an agent may call it unprompted; person-only = the person's own judgment is the point, so an agent runs it only on a file the person supplied and says so
conventions.cost: free = local; gpu = calls the djev Cloud Run GPU ($3.19/h while up, about 2 min cold start); ask the person before a run expected to exceed about $2

tools.name: djp.status
tools.description: The single perception act: every customer, its live release, holdout accuracy vs the bar, per-question backend, and whether new labels have arrived since (stale).

tools.name: djp.init
tools.description: Create an empty customer (customer.json with placeholders) in $DJP_HOME.

tools.name: djp.import
tools.description: Replace the customer's labelled rows with a CSV/JSONL in their own column names. Adds questions (options from the data) that customer.json lacks.
tools.why_person_only: The labels are the ground truth every gate is judged against. An agent that wrote them could pass its own gate. An agent may run it only on a file the person supplied.

label.description: columns holding the answers, one per question

tools.name: djp.check
tools.description: Validate customer.json and data.jsonl: options, missing answers, holdout size, rows per option. No model calls.

tools.name: djp.eval
tools.description: Every candidate of every arm on the holdout, per question (accuracy/log-loss), and what the gate would pick. Writes no release; fills the read caches.
tools.cost: gpu if arms include djev and rows are not cached; else free

tools.name: djp.release
tools.description: Candidates -> per-question gate (accuracy >= bar and log-loss < bar) -> release record + tiny weights -> CURRENT. UNCHANGED when the live release was built from the same data and arms.
tools.cost: gpu if arms include djev and rows are not cached; else free

tools.name: djp.label
tools.description: Append new labelled rows (dedup by text; conflicting labels refused), then retrain tiny, gate, and move CURRENT only on pass. Re-running with the same file changes nothing.
tools.cost: gpu for new holdout rows if the live release uses djev; else free
tools.why_person_only: New labels are new ground truth for the gate. An agent may run it only on a file the person labelled.

tools.name: djp.rollback
tools.description: Point CURRENT at an earlier release that passed its gate (default: the one before the live one). Takes effect on the server's next request.

tools.name: serve.answer
tools.description: Answer one text for a customer on its live release; each answer names its backend.
tools.cost: gpu if a question is on djev; else free

tools.name: serve.release
tools.description: The live release for a customer as the server sees it: version, bar, per-question backend and holdout accuracy.

tools.name: samples.build
tools.description: Build a stand-in customer from public Hugging Face data (shop, helpdesk, moderation); prints the import command.

tools.name: ab.run
tools.description: djev vs GLiNER A/B with the option-order test over every customer holdout + fast-decisions. Resumable.
tools.cost: gpu (the full suite is about 15k calls, about 7 min of GPU); ask above about $2

tools.name: ab.report
tools.description: Markdown aggregates of an A/B run (default: the newest).

tools.name: tiny.banking77
tools.description: Benchmark: Ettin-17M fine-tuned on banking77 (optionally N rows per class), scored on the 3,080-row test set.

tools.name: tiny.customer
tools.description: Benchmark: tiny per question on a customer's training split, scored on their holdout (no release written).
